package_info.package_versions: various versions distributed during the SmoothOperator campaign (March 2023)
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CXDesktopApp installer was trojanized to include a malicious payload that is loaded at runtime, enabling the attacker to beacon to external infrastructure and potentially deliver further malware. This constitutes a supply chain attack, as the legitimate application was modified to include and execute unauthorized code.

execution_context.file_location: DLL loaded by 3CXDesktopApp (e.g., ffmpeg.dll or d3dcompiler_47.dll)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code is loaded as a DLL by the main application, collects system information, and sends a beacon to an attacker-controlled domain via HTTPS, enabling remote command and control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is executed as part of a legitimate application's startup process but performs unauthorized network communication to an external domain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate VoIP application should not load unknown DLLs or beacon to untrusted external infrastructure.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some applications may check for updates or send telemetry, but these should be to trusted vendor domains and be transparent to the user.
key_indicators: Execution within the context of a signed, trusted application

attack_chain.action: User downloads and installs the trojanized 3CXDesktopApp from the official or compromised distribution channel.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious DLL is present on the system.

attack_chain.action: Upon application launch, the malicious DLL is loaded by the main application process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in the context of the trusted application.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code collects system information and beacons to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishes command and control, enabling further malicious activity.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected DLL loading by a signed application
Network beacons to untrusted or newly registered domains at application startup
Collection and exfiltration of system information by a VoIP or communications app
file_indicators: Presence of non-standard or recently modified DLLs in the 3CXDesktopApp installation directory (e.g., ffmpeg.dll, d3dcompiler_47.dll)
Unexpected changes to application binaries or supporting libraries
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS requests to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., domains not associated with 3CX)
Beaconing behavior shortly after application launch
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected DLLs loaded by 3CXDesktopApp, especially those not matching known-good hashes. Inspect network traffic from the application for connections to untrusted or newly registered domains. Alert on collection and exfiltration of system information by the application. Use EDR or AV solutions to detect known malicious variants of the trojanized DLLs.
